Absolute high-end wildlife/editorial photographic realism with truthful fur, grass, stone, hands and mountain light; never a painting, illustration, children’s-book image, plush-toy look or CGI. Research grounding: depict a breed-faithful young Tornjak, the Bosnian and Herzegovinian–Croatian shepherd dog described by FCI Standard No. 355: sturdy, square-built, long dense coat, predominantly white with well-separated dark patches, natural drop ears and an alert but steady livestock-guardian character. The Vlašić setting is a broad high limestone pasture with mixed meadow grasses, scattered gray rock, distant beech/fir forest and rounded upland ridges used for livestock. No alpine fantasy peaks. Main animal: one five-month-old Tornjak puppy, already large-pawed and powerful but unmistakably young, with a thick white coat, a charcoal-black patch over one ear and across the back, a smaller warm-brown marking near the other eye, dark intelligent eyes and a heavy feathered tail. The puppy has just found an oversized lost blue wool mitten. It bounds toward the near camera carrying the mitten proudly, then brakes in surprise, front paws splayed naturally, ears uneven and eyes bright. The face, fur and full body are clear, energetic and immediately memorable. Human relationship: behind and to the side, a distinct 20-year-old Bosnian shepherd woman in a sun-faded crimson overshirt, practical brown trousers and rubber pasture boots crouches beside a simple lamb pen, reaching one open hand toward the puppy. She does not look at the camera; she looks only at the dog with an affectionate, exasperated laugh. Her whole head and hands remain visible, but the puppy is unquestionably the main subject. Two sheep may appear only as soft background context, not additional featured animals. Strong late-afternoon sun from the side/back makes the long white coat glow strand by strand and lights windblown grass seeds; cool sky fill preserves dark fur and human skin. A brief gust lifts fur, overshirt and meadow heads, producing lively depth. Eye-level low camera close to puppy height, dynamic square composition, puppy’s eyes tack sharp, realistic motion and natural shallow depth of field, fine camera grain. No person looking at camera, no posed family portrait, no collar logo, no leash, no show-dog grooming, no Saint Bernard markings or generic fluffy breed, no snow, no resort buildings, no fantasy mountains, no painted softness, no duplicate dogs, no malformed paws/hands, no extra limbs, no text, labels, logos, watermark or border.
